Triggers on draining a Renovate PR backlog, paused Renovate cron, slow CI lockfile regeneration, or "rebase this Renovate PR now without spending Actions minutes."

Pass 1 cancels ALL queued PREVIEW deployments by a given githubLogin (e.g. a CI bot firing a preview per project on every push). Pass 2 cancels queued PRODUCTION deployments by a given githubLogin, keeping the newest per project so the latest code still ships. Use for "sweep the Vercel queue", "drain queued previews", "cancel a bot's preview deploys", "cancel stale prod deploys keep latest per app". Both passes are opt-in via env/config.

---
name: project-env-quirks
description: "Machine/env quirks on Eric's Mac that bite headless agent sessions (docker pulls, biome gate)"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: b10586c9-1b13-412f-92b7-ddd260a6528c
  modified: 2026-07-31T14:16:58.341Z
---

Two environment quirks hit during the knowledge-hub build (2026-07-11):

1. **`docker pull` hangs forever in headless sessions.** `~/.docker/config.json` has `credsStore: "desktop"` plus a Docker Scout hook on `pull`; the credential helper blocks on macOS Keychain without a UI. Even `docker run` hangs at "Unable to find image locally".
   **How to apply:** `mkdir -p /tmp/docker-nocreds && echo '{}' > /tmp/docker-nocreds/config.json`, then `DOCKER_CONFIG=/tmp/docker-nocreds docker pull …` — completes in seconds. `docker ps`/`exec`/`run` (with image present) work normally.

2. **Biome gate (ultracite v7 extends paths): fixed per-branch, not repo-wide.** biome.jsonc must extend `ultracite/biome/*` (v7 layout), not the v5-era `ultracite/core|react|next`; check/fix scripts must run the local ultracite pin, never `@latest`. Applied on Kheirah/agent-knowledge-hub-design (484e1a0 + 26327a7, 2026-07-11) and independently re-derived on Kheirah/continue-prev-task (fe73b90, 2026-07-12) — branches cut before those commits will still show "Could not resolve ultracite/core"; apply the same two-line fix. Repo-wide pre-existing findings remain (hundreds; scoped `bunx biome check <path>` is the usable gate for new work). The masterclass exhibit dir is mechanically clean as of fe73b90 (~36 judgment-rule findings left: noJsxPropsBind, noExportedImports, index keys).
   **Zombie dirty files:** entire.io (manual-commit strategy) snapshots uncommitted changes to a shadow branch and re-applies them post-commit ("carried forward remaining files") — a plain `git checkout --` of unwanted noise gets silently undone at the next commit. Cure: `git checkout -- <files> && entire clean --force` (drops the HEAD shadow branch + session carry-forward state; committed checkpoint history is unaffected).
   Also: Biome's `useSortedKeys` assist auto-sorts object keys on `--write` — it silently reorders semantically-ordered literals (MongoDB compound-index key specs). Guard such files with `// biome-ignore-all assist/source/useSortedKeys: …`.

3. **Vercel:** hasToggle.dev deploys as project `has-toggle-dev-web` under team scope `spiritsdontfly` (not the default `kheirahs-projects`, not `forsuxess`). Use `vercel ls/inspect --scope spiritsdontfly`; `vercel inspect --logs <url>` pulls build logs without switching scope. (2026-07-24)

4. **Bun override staleness:** after adding a root `overrides` entry, plain `bun install` updates `bun.lock` but can leave stale `.bun` store symlinks (nested dep still resolving to the old version). `rm -rf node_modules && bun install` is required for the override to actually take effect. (2026-07-24, radix-slot pin)

5. **The `web` app's locale-prefixed URLs 500 in dev.** `http://localhost:3001/en/learn/...` dies in middleware (`[NEMO] Middleware execution failed`); the unprefixed `http://localhost:3001/learn/...` serves fine. Use the unprefixed path when driving the site in a browser or the masterclass page looks broken when it isn't. `curl` also 500s on both (the middleware chain needs real browser headers) — verify with Playwright/Chrome DevTools, not curl. Next 16 also refuses to start a second dev server for the same project dir ("Run kill <pid> to stop it"), so reuse Eric's running server on 3001 rather than starting your own. (2026-07-25)

6. **Shared `.next` dir: `next build` then `next dev` corrupts some routes.** Running dev after a prod build in the same `apps/web/.next` produces `SyntaxError: Unexpected non-whitespace character after JSON` and 500s on a subset of routes (hit the nuqs-using learn pages, 2026-07-31, Next 16.2 + cacheComponents) while others serve fine. Cure: `rm -rf apps/web/.next` before starting dev. Don't misread the 500s as an app bug — the prod build of the same source passes.

Related: [[project_ts7_migration]]

1	# CLAUDE.md
2	
3	This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.
4	
5	## Overview
6	
7	This is a **has-toggle** monorepo - a production-grade Turborepo template for Next.js SaaS applications. The codebase is built around five core principles: Fast, Cheap, Opinionated, Modern, and Safe. It uses Bun workspaces and Turborepo for managing multiple applications and shared packages.
8	
9	## Development Commands
10	
11	### Setup & Installation
12	```bash
13	bun install                    # Install all dependencies
14	```
15	
16	Set `MONGODB_URI` in the environment (validated via @t3-oss/env-nextjs in `packages/database/keys.ts`).
17	
18	### Running Applications
19	```bash
20	bun dev                       # Run all apps in development mode
21	turbo dev --filter=app         # Run only the main app (port 3000)
22	turbo dev --filter=web         # Run only the web/marketing site (port 3001)
23	turbo dev --filter=api         # Run only the API (port 3002, includes Stripe webhook listener)
24	```
25	
26	### Testing
27	```bash
28	bun test                      # Run tests across all workspaces
29	turbo test --filter=app        # Run tests for specific app
30	bun test                       # Run Bun test runner in apps/app or apps/api
31	```
32	
33	### Code Quality
34	```bash
35	bun run check                     # Run Biome linter/formatter checks (uses ultracite presets)
36	bun run fix                       # Auto-fix linting/formatting issues
37	turbo boundaries               # Check package boundaries
38	```
39	
40	### Building
41	```bash
42	bun run build                     # Build all apps (depends on tests passing)
43	turbo build --filter=app       # Build specific app
44	turbo analyze --filter=app     # Analyze bundle size
45	```
46	
47	### Database
48

1	# CLAUDE.md
2	
3	This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.
4	
5	## Overview
6	
7	This is a **has-toggle** monorepo - a production-grade Turborepo template for Next.js SaaS applications. The codebase is built around five core principles: Fast, Cheap, Opinionated, Modern, and Safe. It uses Bun workspaces and Turborepo for managing multiple applications and shared packages.
8	
9	## Development Commands
10	
11	### Setup & Installation
12	```bash
13	bun install                    # Install all dependencies
14	```
15	
16	Set `MONGODB_URI` in the environment (validated via @t3-oss/env-nextjs in `packages/database/keys.ts`).
17	
18	### Running Applications
19	```bash
20	bun dev                       # Run all apps in development mode
21	turbo dev --filter=app         # Run only the main app (port 3000)
22	turbo dev --filter=web         # Run only the web/marketing site (port 3001)
23	turbo dev --filter=api         # Run only the API (port 3002, includes Stripe webhook listener)
24	```
25	
26	### Testing
27	```bash
28	bun test                      # Run tests across all workspaces
29	turbo test --filter=app        # Run tests for specific app
30	bun test                       # Run Bun test runner in apps/app or apps/api
31	```
32	
33	### Code Quality
34	```bash
35	bun run check                     # Run Biome linter/formatter checks (uses ultracite presets)
36	bun run fix                       # Auto-fix linting/formatting issues
37	turbo boundaries               # Check package boundaries
38	```
39	
40	### Building
41	```bash
42	bun run build                     # Build all apps (depends on tests passing)
43	turbo build --filter=app       # Build specific app
44	turbo analyze --filter=app     # Analyze bundle size
45	```
46	
47	### Database
48	
49	The database is MongoDB, accessed through the official `mongodb` driver — there is no ORM, no schema migrations, and no generated client. `packages/database/index.ts` exports a `database` object with typed collection handles; document types live in `packages/database/types.ts`.
50	
51	### Maintenance
52	```bash
53	bun run bump-deps                 # Update dependencies (excludes recharts)
54	bun run bump-ui                   # Update shadcn/ui components
55	bun run clean                     # Clean node_modules from root
56	turbo clean                    # Clean build artifacts and node_modules from all workspaces
57	```
58	
59	## Architecture
60	
61	### Monorepo Structure
62	
63	The repository uses **Bun workspaces** with two main directories:
64	
65	- **apps/** - Deployable applications (independently deployable)
66	- **packages/** - Shared packages consumed by apps
67	
68	### Applications (apps/)
69	
70	1. **app** (port 3000) - Main SaaS application
71	   - Authentication via better-auth (route groups: `(authenticated)` and `(unauthenticated)`); handler mounted at `/api/auth/[...all]`
72	   - Uses Next.js 16 with App Router
73	   - Server actions in `app/actions/`
74	   - API routes in `app/api/`
75	   - Tests configured with Bun test runner
76	
77	2. **web** (port 3001) - Marketing/landing page
78	   - Internationalization support (uses `[locale]` route)
79	   - Content management via CMS package
80	   - Rate limiting via Arcjet
81	
82	3. **api** (port 3002) - RESTful API server
83	   - Health check endpoint at `/health`
84	   - Webhook handlers in `app/webhooks/`
85	   - Cron jobs in `app/cron/`
86	   - Development includes Stripe webhook listener (requires Stripe CLI)
87	
88	4. **docs** - Documentation site (Mintlify)
89	5. **email** - Email templates (React Email)
90	6. **storybook** (`apps/storybook`) - Component development environment.
91	   Its package name is `@repo/storybook`, **not** `storybook`: Bun links every
92	   workspace package into the root `node_modules` by name, so a workspace named
93	   `storybook` shadows the real `storybook` npm package and every addon that
94	   imports `storybook/internal/*` fails to resolve. Turbo filter is
95	   `--filter=@repo/storybook`. Never name a workspace after one of its own
96	   dependencies.
97	7. **studio** - Database management UI (stale Prisma Studio wrapper; non-functional since the MongoDB migration)
98	
99	### Shared Packages (packages/)
100	
101	Core infrastructure packages:
102	
103	- **@repo/auth** - better-auth authentication (client, server, middleware, provider)
104	  - MongoDB adapter + organization plugin; the active org id is the tenant id
105	  - Server instance in `instance.ts`; `server.ts` is a Clerk-shaped compat layer
106	    (`auth()`, `currentUser()`) so callers did not have to change
107	  - Handler mounted by apps/app at `/api/auth/[...all]`
108	- **@repo/database** - MongoDB via the official `mongodb` driver (server-only)
109	  - Typed collection handles exported from `packages/database/index.ts`
110	  - Document types at `packages/database/types.ts`
111	  - Requires `MONGODB_URI` (validated in `packages/database/keys.ts`)
112	- **@repo/design-system** - shadcn/ui component library
113	  - Components in `components/` (auto-generated, excluded from Biome linting)
114	  - Providers for themes, tooltips, etc.
115	  - Dark mode support via next-themes
116	- **@repo/observability** - Sentry error tracking and logging
117	- **@repo/security** - Arcjet integration for application security
118	- **@repo/analytics** - Google Analytics and PostHog
119	- **@repo/payments** - Stripe integration
120	- **@repo/email** - Resend email service
121	- **@repo/webhooks** - Webhook handling (inbound/outbound)
122	- **@repo/collaboration** - Real-time features (Liveblocks)
123	- **@repo/feature-flags** - Feature flag management
124	- **@repo/notifications** - In-app notifications
125	- **@repo/internationalization** - i18n support
126	- **@repo/cms** - Content management (BaseHub)
127	- **@repo/seo** - SEO utilities
128	- **@repo/storage** - File upload/management
129	- **@repo/ai** - AI integration utilities
130	
131	### Technology Stack
132	
133	- **Framework**: Next.js 16 with App Router, React 19
134	- **Language**: TypeScript 5.9 (strict mode, NodeNext module resolution)
135	- **Package Manager**: Bun 1.1.43
136	- **Build Tool**: Turborepo 2.5.8
137	- **Database**: MongoDB via the official `mongodb` driver 7.x
138	- **Auth**: better-auth (email/password + organizations)
139	- **Styling**: Tailwind CSS 4.1
140	- **Linting**: Biome 2.3.1 with ultracite presets (core, react, next)
141	- **Testing**: Bun test runner
142	- **Bundling**: tsup for package builds
143	
144	### Important Patterns
145	
146	1. **Workspace Dependencies**: Internal packages use `workspace:*` protocol
147	   - Example: `"@repo/auth": "workspace:*"`
148	
149	2. **Route Groups**: Apps use Next.js route groups for layout separation
150	   - app: `(authenticated)` and `(unauthenticated)` groups
151	   - web: `[locale]` for internationalization
152	
153	3. **Server/Client Separation**: Packages use `server-only` for server-side code
154	   - Database and auth server utilities are server-only
155	   - Client components/utilities are separate files
156	
157	4. **Environment Variables**: Uses @t3-oss/env-nextjs for type-safe env validation
158	
159	5. **Path Aliases**: Apps configure aliases via tsconfig.json paths
160	   - `@/` - points to app root
161	   - `@repo/` - points to packages directory
162	
163	6. **Biome Exclusions**: Auto-generated code excluded from linting:
164	   - `packages/design-system/components/ui` (shadcn components)
165	   - `packages/collaboration/config.ts` (Liveblocks config)
166	   - `packages/cms/basehub-types.d.ts` (CMS types)
167	
168	7. **Build Dependencies**: `turbo.json` configures build to depend on tests passing
169	   - Builds run `^build` (dependency builds) then `test` before building
170	
171	## Key Files
172	
173	- `turbo.json` - Turborepo task pipeline configuration
174	- `biome.jsonc` - Linter/formatter configuration (extends ultracite presets)
175	- `packages/database/types.ts` - Database document types
176	- Root `package.json` - Monorepo scripts, workspace configuration, and CLI entry point (`dist/index.js`)
177	
178	## Development Notes
179

content.thinking: These are false positives from Biome's type inference around refs — it can't track assignments through JSX, so `useRef<T | null>(null)` gets narrowed to just `null`. These need `biome-ignore` comments rather than actual code changes, since removing the guards would break things at runtime. I should check how other projects handled this same rule to see what approach they took.

content.text:
All applied and verified. Everything is uncommitted on `Kheirah/port-memorynine-changes`.

## What I ported

**better-auth migration** (fork's `a5c96780` + follow-up `b576e7b8`)
- `@repo/auth` is now better-auth on the MongoDB adapter with the organization plugin. New `instance.ts` (server instance + `authDb`), a Clerk-shaped compat layer in `server.ts` (`auth()`, `currentUser()`, `listOrganizationMembers()`, `getUserByStripeCustomerId()`) so no caller had to change, and hand-built `SignIn`/`SignUp`/`UserButton`/`OrganizationSwitcher` components.
- Handler mounted at `apps/app/app/api/auth/[...all]`. `apps/api/app/webhooks/auth/route.ts` (Clerk/svix) deleted; the Stripe webhook now looks users up by `user.stripeCustomerId`. `img.clerk.com` dropped from `next-config`.
- **Adapted for this repo:** `instance.ts` uses `client.db()` — the same call `@repo/database` makes — rather than the fork's `MONGODB_DB ?? "app"`. I also skipped the fork's `migrate-to-app-db.ts`, which only exists to move memorynine's live auth data.

**Lint & storybook**
- `apps/storybook` renamed to `@repo/storybook`. Verified the shadowing was real here: on `origin/main`, `node_modules/storybook` symlinked to `apps/storybook@0.1.0`; it now resolves to `storybook@10.5.7`. Turbo filter is `--filter=@repo/storybook`.
- `bun run check` went from **774 errors to 0**. 156 of the fork's 183 lint-fixed files were byte-identical to our pre-lint state, so I took their fixed versions verbatim; the remaining ~26 findings (mostly in the `(playground)` files that PR #337 added after the fork) I fixed by hand using the fork's stated conventions — `useCallback`, `cond ? x : null`, `ref.current !== null`, extracted row components.

**Other changes I judged we needed**
- Biome no longer reformats SVGs (this was what dirtied `apps/docs/*.svg` in your working tree on every run) + the `.claude` format hook.
- `scripts/skip-ci.js` — the `ignoreCommand` in all four `vercel.json` files pointed at a file that never existed and "worked" only because node exits 1 on a missing file. Fixed the path (`../../scripts/skip-ci.js`) in all four, not just the two the fork fixed.
- `@react-email/components` → `react-email`; dropped unused `@react-email/preview-server` and `@clerk/types`.
- `@rescale/nemo` → `@zanreal/nemo` (the maintained fork).
- `@source` entries so Tailwind scans the auth and notifications packages — without this the new auth menus render with missing classes.
- MongoDB connection-pool sizing in `@repo/database` (`maxPoolSize: 5` et al).

## Verification

`bun run check` clean · `turbo typecheck` 24/24 · `turbo test` 189 pass, 0 fail · `app`, `web`, `api` all build, `/api/auth/[...all]` present in the route table.

**One failure, pre-existing:** `@repo/storybook build` fails on `@storybook/nextjs` having no `./preset` export. I checked out `origin/main` in a scratch worktree — it fails identically there. Not caused by this work; it's an upstream packaging bug.

## Deliberately not ported — your call

1. **`MONGODB_DB ?? "app"` database rename.** The fork renamed off the driver's implicit `test` default after confirming their collections were empty. Yours aren't — `subscribers`/`digests` hold live waitlist data. That's a migration, not a config change. Left as `client.db()` with a comment, in both `@repo/database` and the new auth instance.
2. **Self-hosted Renovate workflow** (`09c87c94`, `5243fb39`, `fc4a9f4d` + `docs/renovate.md`). You're on the hosted Renovate app here; adding the workflow would double up.
3. **Deleting `.github/workflows/claude-code-review.yml`.** Preference, not a fix.
4. **Removing Liveblocks / `@repo/collaboration`.** The fork called it "never part of this stack", but `apps/app` still uses it (`AvatarStack`, `Cursors`, the collaboration auth route). Removing it is a product decision.
5. Everything memorynine-specific: knowledge hub, eval suite, capture/review UI, eve integration, their landing page and brand.

**Before deploying:** set `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET` (≥32 chars) and `BETTER_AUTH_URL` in Vercel, and the `CLERK_*` / `NEXT_PUBLIC_CLERK_*` vars can go — including the stale ones still sitting in `apps/web/.env.local`. Existing Clerk users won't carry over; better-auth starts with an empty `user` collection.

feat: port better-auth, the lint sweep and shared infra fixes from memorynine

The memorynine fork diverged at 4702dbc0 and fixed a number of things that
belong here too. This brings back everything that is not memorynine's own
product work.

better-auth replaces Clerk (fork's a5c96780 + b576e7b8). @repo/auth is now
better-auth on the MongoDB adapter with the organization plugin: a server
instance in instance.ts, a Clerk-shaped compat layer in server.ts (auth(),
currentUser(), listOrganizationMembers(), getUserByStripeCustomerId()) so no
caller had to change, and hand-built SignIn/SignUp/UserButton/
OrganizationSwitcher components. The handler mounts at
/api/auth/[...all]. The Clerk/svix webhook route is gone and the Stripe
webhook looks users up by user.stripeCustomerId instead of walking Clerk's
privateMetadata.

Two deliberate departures from the fork: instance.ts calls client.db(), the
same call @repo/database makes, rather than MONGODB_DB ?? "app" — this repo's
subscribers and digests hold live data under the driver's implicit default, so
renaming the database is a migration and not a config change. The fork's
migrate-to-app-db.ts script only exists to move memorynine's own auth data and
is not ported.

The lint gate was reporting 774 errors and now reports none. 156 of the fork's
183 lint-fixed files were byte-identical to ours pre-lint, so those are taken
verbatim; the remainder — mostly the (playground) files #337 added after the
fork point — are fixed here by hand using the same conventions the fork
settled on: useCallback for handler props, `cond ? x : null` for conditional
JSX, `ref.current !== null` where biome reads useRef(null).current as
always-null, and an extracted component where a handler closed over a .map
item. Behaviour is unchanged.

apps/storybook is renamed to @repo/storybook. The shadowing was real here:
on main, node_modules/storybook symlinked to apps/storybook@0.1.0 rather than
storybook@10.5.7. Turbo filter is now --filter=@repo/storybook.

Also ported:

- biome no longer formats SVGs, which was rewriting apps/docs/*.svg on every
  run
- scripts/skip-ci.js now exists. Every vercel.json named a file that never
  did, and builds proceeded only because node exits 1 on a missing file, which
  Vercel reads as "build". Fixed in all four apps, not just the two the fork
  needed
- @react-email/components -> react-email; dropped @react-email/preview-server
  and @clerk/types
- @rescale/nemo -> @zanreal/nemo
- @source entries so Tailwind scans the auth and notifications packages —
  without them the new auth menus render with classes that were never
  generated
- connection-pool sizing on the shared MongoDB client

check, typecheck and test are green; app, web and api all build. The
@repo/storybook build fails on @storybook/nextjs shipping no ./preset export
condition — verified identical on origin/main, so it is not from this work.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF

- `server.ts` — a Clerk-shaped compat layer (`auth()`, `currentUser()`, `listOrganizationMembers()`, `getUserByStripeCustomerId()`), so **no caller had to change**
- Hand-built `SignIn` / `SignUp` / `UserButton` / `OrganizationSwitcher`, keeping the prop shapes the sidebar already passes
- Handler mounts at `/api/auth/[...all]`
- The Clerk/svix webhook route is gone; the Stripe webhook looks users up by `user.stripeCustomerId` instead of walking Clerk's `privateMetadata`

**Two deliberate departures from the fork.** `instance.ts` calls `client.db()` — the same call `@repo/database` makes — rather than `MONGODB_DB ?? "app"`. This repo's `subscribers` and `digests` hold live data under the driver's implicit default, so renaming the database is a migration, not a config change. And the fork's `migrate-to-app-db.ts` only exists to move memorynine's own auth data, so it isn't ported.

## The lint gate

`bun run check` was reporting **774 errors** and now reports none.

156 of the fork's 183 lint-fixed files were byte-identical to ours pre-lint, so those are taken verbatim. The remainder — mostly the `(playground)` files #337 added after the fork point — are fixed here by hand, using the conventions the fork settled on: `useCallback` for handler props, `cond ? x : null` for conditional JSX, `ref.current !== null` where biome reads `useRef(null).current` as always-null, and an extracted component where a handler closed over a `.map` item. **PR #360:** https://github.com/hasToggle/hasToggle.dev/pull/360

## The two env vars

**Secret:**
```bash
openssl rand -base64 32
```
That gives 44 characters; `packages/auth/keys.ts` requires at least 32, so it clears the bar. Set it as `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET`.

**URL:** `BETTER_AUTH_URL` is the origin of whichever app mounts the handler — that's `apps/app`, so it's the same value you already have in `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL`. Origin only, no path: better-auth appends `/api/auth` itself.

- Local: `http://localhost:3000`
- Production: your app's domain, e.g. `https://app.hastoggle.dev`

Both are declared `.optional()` in `keys.ts` so builds without them still pass — better-auth itself refuses to run in production without a secret, which is the check that actually matters. `localhost:3000/3001/3002` are already in `trustedOrigins`.

For preview deployments the URL differs per deployment, so either leave `BETTER_AUTH_URL` unset there and let better-auth infer from the request, or point it at a stable preview alias.

## Commit and PR

One commit, 228 files, `+3222/−2238`, pushed to `origin/Kheirah/port-memorynine-changes`. The PR body carries the full breakdown, the two deliberate departures from the fork, the list of what I left out and why, and the verification results — including the note that the `@repo/storybook` build failure is upstream and reproduces identically on `main`.
